official_measurement_examples.name: Approved Document K scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Approved Document K covers stairs, ladders, ramps, guarding, vehicle barriers, glazing and other protections from falling, collision and impact.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2012 publication framework
official_measurement_examples.fact: Circular 02/2012 announced the new Approved Document K and transitional Building Regulations changes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Glazing integration
official_measurement_examples.fact: The 2013 Approved Document K incorporated glazing safety material formerly associated with Approved Document N.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 39 appeal scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Building Act section 39 appeal decisions address the facts of a specific relaxation or dispensation dispute and are not automatic rules for other projects.

official_measurement_examples.name: Headroom case specificity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Published K1 stair appeals show that headroom and stair geometry are assessed in the particular building context rather than converted into parcel development capacity.

official_measurement_examples.name: Guarding versus planning
official_measurement_examples.fact: Guarding and barrier compliance is a Building Regulations safety matter and does not itself grant planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Local authority summaries
official_measurement_examples.fact: Official council guidance presents Part K as one Building Regulations topic and keeps Building Regulations separate from town planning.

official_measurement_examples.name: Ownership separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Part K safety compliance does not determine ownership, title boundaries or rights to use adjoining land.

core_rules: Approved Document K compliance is not planning permission
planning permission is not Part K compliance
section 39 relaxation appeal is case-specific and not a universal rule
stair geometry evidence is not parcel development capacity
guarding compliance is not land-title evidence
safety glazing compliance is not planning condition discharge unless the decision says so
vehicle barrier compliance is not highway access approval
loading-bay protection is not transport-planning approval
historic Approved Document N glazing guidance must not override current Part K without date checking
local authority summary is not a project-specific building-control decision
product test evidence is not proof of correct installation
Building Regulations completion is not planning permission
Part K compliance does not create access or maintenance rights over adjoining land
appeal outcome for one building must not be promoted to another parcel
NO_DATA must remain NO_DATA rather than no falling or collision constraint
no parcel Part K clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
